es.summary: Debilidad o daño de los músculos y tejido conectivo del suelo pélvico que produce incontinencia, prolapso y dolor pélvico.
key_points: El embarazo y el parto vaginal son los principales desencadenantes.
Obesidad, envejecimiento y tos crónica aumentan la presión intraabdominal.
El entrenamiento de los músculos del suelo pélvico es la primera línea de tratamiento.
Complicaciones incluyen infecciones urinarias recurrentes y deterioro de la calidad de vida.

pathophysiology: Debilidad de músculos y ligamentos del suelo pélvico.
Pérdida de soporte a útero, vejiga y recto.
Descenso de órganos (prolapso) y pérdida de continencia.
risk_factors: Embarazo y parto vaginal, especialmente con episiotomía.
Obesidad y aumento de presión intraabdominal.
Tos crónica, estreñimiento y levantamiento de cargas pesadas.
signs_symptoms: Incontinencia urinaria de esfuerzo o urgencia.
Sensación de presión o bulto en la vagina.
Disfunción sexual y sensación de pesadez.
diagnostics: Estudios urodinámicos para evaluar la función vesical.
treatment: Entrenamiento de los músculos del suelo pélvico (ejercicios de Kegel).
Biofeedback o estimulación eléctrica para mejorar la contracción.
Uso de pesario vaginal en casos de prolapso moderado.
Terapia de estrógenos locales en mujeres postmenopáusicas.
Cirugía reparadora (colporrafia, sacrocolpopexia) cuando es necesario.
complications: Úlceras por irritación o dermatitis perineal.
Disfunción sexual y disminución de la autoestima.
nursing_care: Evaluar tipo y frecuencia de incontinencia y prolapso.
Realizar inspección de piel perineal y registrar lesiones.
Enseñar y supervisar ejercicios de Kegel con biofeedback.
Registrar ingesta y eliminación; fomentar hidratación adecuada.
Colaborar con fisioterapeuta para programa de fortalecimiento.
patient_teaching: Practicar ejercicios de Kegel 3 series de 10 repeticiones, 3 veces al día.
Mantener peso corporal saludable y evitar esfuerzos excesivos.
Controlar el estreñimiento con fibra dietética y suficiente líquido.
Usar productos absorbentes discretos y cambiar con frecuencia.
Buscar atención médica ante aumento del prolapso o infecciones.

outcomes: Alivio del dolor: puntuación ≤3 en escala de 0‑10
Participación en actividades diarias sin limitación

interventions.action: Evaluar la intensidad del dolor usando escala numérica cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Permite monitorear la respuesta al tratamiento y ajustar intervenciones.

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de relajación y respiración diafragmática
interventions.rationale: Reduce la percepción del dolor mediante control del sistema nervioso autónomo.

interventions.action: Aplicar calor local en zona lumbar/pélvica según tolerancia
interventions.rationale: El calor aumenta el flujo sanguíneo y disminuye la espasticidad muscular.

interventions.action: Facilitar la práctica de ejercicios de Kegel con biofeedback
interventions.rationale: Fortalece el suelo pélvico y disminuye el dolor asociado al prolapso.

interventions.action: Coordinar con el médico para analgesia adecuada (p. ej., paracetamol, AINE)
interventions.rationale: Control farmacológico complementa las medidas no farmacológicas.

outcomes: Sin lesiones cutáneas en zona perineal durante la hospitalización
Integridad de la piel mantenida según valoración diaria

interventions.action: Inspeccionar piel perineal y áreas de presión cada 8 h
interventions.rationale: Detecta precozmente irritación o úlceras para intervenir a tiempo.

interventions.action: Mantener la zona perineal limpia y seca; usar apósitos absorbentes adecuados
interventions.rationale: Previene maceración y dermatitis asociada a la incontinencia.

interventions.action: Promover cambios de posición cada 2 h y ejercicios de movilidad ligera
interventions.rationale: Reduce la presión prolongada y mejora la circulación periférica.

interventions.action: Aplicar crema protectora con óxido de zinc en piel irritada
interventions.rationale: Crea barrera que protege contra la humedad y fricción.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre uso correcto de dispositivos de absorción y técnicas de higiene
interventions.rationale: Fomenta autocuidado y disminuye factores de riesgo de lesión.

en.summary: Weakness or damage to the muscles and connective tissue of the pelvic floor that causes incontinence, prolapse, and pelvic pain.
key_points: Pregnancy and vaginal delivery are the main triggers.
Obesity, aging, and chronic cough increase intra-abdominal pressure.
Pelvic floor muscle training is the first-line treatment.
Complications include recurrent urinary tract infections and reduced quality of life.

pathophysiology: Weakness of pelvic floor muscles and ligaments.
Loss of support to the uterus, bladder, and rectum.
Descent of organs (prolapse) and loss of continence.
risk_factors: Pregnancy and vaginal delivery, especially with episiotomy.
Chronic cough, constipation, and heavy lifting.
signs_symptoms: Feeling of pressure or bulge in the vagina.
Persistent pelvic or lower back pain.
Sexual dysfunction and feeling of heaviness.
diagnostics: Urodynamic studies to assess bladder function.
treatment: Biofeedback or electrical stimulation to improve contraction.
Use of vaginal pessary in moderate prolapse cases.
Local estrogen therapy in postmenopausal women.
complications: Ulcers from irritation or perineal dermatitis.
Secondary urinary retention due to obstruction.
nursing_care: Assess type and frequency of incontinence and prolapse.
Perform perineal skin inspection and document lesions.
Teach and supervise Kegel exercises with biofeedback.
Record intake and output; encourage adequate hydration.
Collaborate with physiotherapist for strengthening program.
patient_teaching: Practice Kegel exercises 3 sets of 10 repetitions, 3 times daily.
Maintain healthy body weight and avoid excessive strain.
Manage constipation with dietary fiber and adequate fluid intake.
Use discreet absorbent products and change frequently.
Seek medical care if prolapse worsens or infections occur.

outcomes: Participation in daily activities without limitation

interventions.action: Assess pain intensity using numeric scale every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Allows monitoring of treatment response and adjustment of interventions.

interventions.action: Teach relaxation and diaphragmatic breathing techniques
interventions.rationale: Reduces pain perception through autonomic nervous system control.

interventions.action: Apply local heat to lumbar/pelvic area as tolerated
interventions.rationale: Heat increases blood flow and reduces muscle spasticity.

interventions.action: Facilitate Kegel exercise practice with biofeedback
interventions.rationale: Strengthens pelvic floor and reduces pain associated with prolapse.

interventions.action: Coordinate with physician for adequate analgesia (e.g., acetaminophen, NSAIDs)
interventions.rationale: Pharmacologic control complements non-pharmacologic measures.

outcomes: No skin lesions in perineal area during hospitalization
Skin integrity maintained per daily assessment

interventions.action: Inspect perineal skin and pressure areas every 8 h
interventions.rationale: Early detection of irritation or ulcers for timely intervention.

interventions.action: Keep perineal area clean and dry; use appropriate absorbent dressings
interventions.rationale: Prevents maceration and dermatitis associated with incontinence.

interventions.action: Promote position changes every 2 h and light mobility exercises
interventions.rationale: Reduces prolonged pressure and improves peripheral circulation.

interventions.action: Apply zinc oxide protective cream to irritated skin
interventions.rationale: Creates barrier that protects against moisture and friction.

interventions.action: Educate patient on correct use of absorbent devices and hygiene techniques
interventions.rationale: Encourages self-care and reduces injury risk factors.

sources.name: Maternal-Newborn Nursing: Factors Influencing the Process of Labor and Birth

summary.0.quote: Relaxation of the pelvic floor muscles and connective tissue can cause the organs to sag ( pelvic organ prolapse ) and can interfere with their function, causing pain, leaking of urine or stool, constipation, feelings of fullness in the vagina, and difficulty in defecating.

key_points.3.quote: All of these conditions may lead to frequent urinary tract infections.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: For laboring people with previous pelvic floor damage or multiple births, weakness of the muscles can allow for malposition leading to dysfunctional labor.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: The pelvic floor is the term applied to the group of muscles that provide support to the organs located in the pelvis.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: Relaxation of the pelvic floor muscles and connective tissue can cause the organs to sag ( pelvic organ prolapse ) and can interfere with their function, causing pain, leaking of urine or stool, constipation, feelings of fullness in the vagina, and difficulty in defecating.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Signs may include vaginal pressure or a feeling of fullness.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: The patient may experience lower back pain and decreased sexual satisfaction.

sections.diagnostics.1.quote: Diagnostic testing , such as cystoscopy, urodynamics, and colonoscopy, can also assist in diagnosing severity of the issue.

sections.treatment.0.quote: Kegel exercise s are very effective at strengthening the pelvic floor.

sections.complications.0.quote: All of these conditions may lead to frequent urinary tract infections.
